claims.claim: Place de la Bourse marks Bordeaux's 18th-century opening from a walled medieval city toward a classical riverfront.
Part of Bordeaux's 18th-century prosperity came from colonial goods produced through enslaved labor, with slave-trading profits also contributing.
The Miroir d'eau is a modern 2006 intervention, not an 18th-century feature.
Porte Cailhau was built 1493-1496, combines defensive functions with commemorative and early-Renaissance architecture, and recalls Charles VIII's Italian campaign.
Grosse Cloche was a civic belfry and defensive gate, also used as a prison; its current bell dates from 1775 and weighs about 7.75 tonnes.
Saint-André is a multi-century cathedral; the detached Pey-Berland tower began in 1440 and only received bells centuries later.
Aliénor d'Aquitaine married the future Louis VII at Saint-André in 1137; Anne of Austria and Louis XIII married there centuries later.
Grand Théâtre was inaugurated on 7 April 1780, designed by Victor Louis, after nearly seven years of work.
Its façade has 12 Corinthian columns topped by 9 muses and 3 goddesses.
